newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian soymeal buoyed by export demand.
newsitem.headline: Indian soymeal buoyed by export demand.

text.p: Indian soymeal prices are being lifted by export demand and recent trends in international markets, traders said on Tuesday.
Soymeal was quoted at $305-306 per tonne fas (free alongside ship) in bulk, compared with $292 in the previous week and $218-220 a year ago.
"Indian soymeal prices may further go up as availability was poor due to low processing in India as soybean arrivals was very poor," said S.N. Saboo of trading firm S.S. Mercantile.
"Bullish trends in Indian soymeal will continue," said another trader.
Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) March soymeal futures set an 8-1/2 year high on Monday on fund buying.

Traders in the central Indian city of Indore said around two million tonnes of soymeal had already been traded for the 1996/97 (Nov-Oct) season. They expect another half a million to be traded by the end of the season.
India had traded 1.8 million tonnes of soymeal at this time last year.
They said high world prices might hasten sales of the remaining 0.5 million by June. Last year trading in soymeal continued up to October.
India hopes to export about 2.3 million tonnes of soymeal in 1996/97, the same as in the previous season.
Daily soybean arrivals in the markets had dwindled to 1,800 tonnes against 15,000 at the same time last year.
Soybeans in Indian markets were quoted at 12,000-12,600 rupees a tonne compared with 10,000-10,400 at the same time last year.
